newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UM H1 96 seen better but doubts remain.
newsitem.headline: UM H1 96 seen better but doubts remain.

text.p: Belgian non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere (UM) is expected to unveil later on Tuesday a sharp improvement in group net profit for the first half of the year, analysts said.
But doubts remain over its ability to fully and smoothly institute its major restructuring plan, making the current share price of 2,385 francs look a little toppy, they warned.
Estimates of current group net profit for the six months to June 30 ranged between 600 and 700 million francs compared to 311 million in the same 1995 period.
Analyst Thierry Hazevoets of Generale Bank put the figure at 600 million francs.

He calculated that high zinc refining margins, a positive dollar effect and strong premiums of UM selling prices over London Metals Exchange prices would more than offset the adverse effects of bad weather earlier this year on the construction industry's demand for zinc.

"The refining results will improve by 700 million francs but the metal transforming side will decline by 400 million," Hazevoets said, noting this meant a net 300 million francs improvement in the bottom line.

He noted there were no mining activities to affect the figures. No major changes were expected from copper. He said the results from recycling were very difficult to predict, with a possible stock change impact.
Isabelle Defrane of Mignon, Hanart, Declerck put full year group net profit at 1.9 billion francs against 1.8 billion in 1995, with the first half of around 700 million francs.
She pointed to the positive dollar effect, the fact that zinc prices had stabilized and some early impact of the restructuring -- although the full effect would not be felt in the figures until 1997.
She said that in the short term the share price could benefit from the effect of re-weightings in the Bel-20 index.

But in common with Hazevoets and Kredietbank's Jan Holvoet, she said the longer-term future of the share -- which has wobbled between a 1996 low of 1,970 francs and a high of 2,450 -- depended on the restructuring plan.
Hazevoets rates the share a 'hold' at 2,400 and a possible 'sell' thereafter.
Holvoet was less positive. "We have a slightly negative rating on the stock at the moment," he said.
